### Theme 1 — Early vocabulary corrections: rejecting "fractal topology," separating Zero from Focus
`[S2705]` — 5 rows condensed into this theme (all of S2705's contributions to this label). Rejects "fractal topology" as too strong (implying unestablished self-similarity/topology/infinite recursion); separates Zero (a claim about influence) from Focus/projection (a choice about what to observe); corrects an assumed Compression(Zoom(x))=x inverse relationship, since compression is lossy in general; replaces causal language ("query forces a zoom") with a testable necessity condition ExpansionNecessary(Q,x); and warns against calling Zero/Focus/Zoom/Surface "operational primitives" before irreducibility/derivability is tested.

### Theme 2 — The founding recursive-zoom operation
`[S2707]` — 4 rows condensed into this theme (all of S2707's contributions to this label). States the founding recursive-zoom operation (a value x observed via Focus can be re-based via Zoom(K,x)=K_x into a new investigable state); states that neutralizing dimensions at one resolution level says nothing about whether those dimensions' finer-resolution structure disappears; gives a worked example of recursive re-basing in ordinary reasoning (a single named factor becoming the object of further inquiry); and explicitly holds the claim of infinite recursive refinement as an open, separately-testable hypothesis rather than a mathematical certainty.
